query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloys (HEAs) exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion (tribocorrosion), resistance is governed by the competition between mechanical depassivation and electrochemical repassivation of a Cr-rich passive film; specifically, shorter repassivation time constants (and a mechanically robust, low-cation-diffusivity passive film) reduce the synergy term between wear and corrosion. Short-range chemical order (SRO) in the HEA substrate acts as the lever that lowers cation mobility and stabilizes a harder, adherent Cr-rich oxide, thereby decreasing both corrosion currents and mechanically assisted film removal, which in turn lowers total material loss under tribocorrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy (e.g., Co-Cr-Fe-Ni family), polycrystalline, solutionized to maximize chemical randomness, similar grain size and surface finish across samples, no second-phase carbides or intermetallics present.
generation.intervention: Induce short-range chemical order in the same composition via low-to-intermediate temperature aging (versus solutionized/random state) while controlling grain size and surface finish to remain matched.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature aerated chloride aqueous environment (e.g., NaCl), reciprocating sliding against an inert counterbody (e.g., alumina) at moderate normal load and speed, fixed potential or open-circuit potential, identical exposure duration for all samples.
generation.structural_mediator: A Cr-rich passive film (chromia/spinel-like) with low cation diffusivity, high hardness, and good adhesion to an SRO-strengthened substrate; the SRO-induced local chemical ordering and lattice friction reduce cation transport and enhance substrate work-hardening that mechanically supports the film.
generation.mechanism: Mechanical sliding periodically removes or thins the passive film (depassivation). The substrate’s SRO increases the rate and integrity of repassivation by promoting rapid Cr enrichment and forming a denser, harder oxide with slower ionic transport. When the repassivation time constant is shorter than the interval between mechanical removal events, the film remains largely intact, lowering corrosion currents and decreasing abrasive/adhesive wear at the interface. This reduces the positive synergy term between wear and corrosion and thus the total tribocorrosion rate.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the solutionized/random baseline, the SRO-treated HEA will show: (a) lower total mass-loss rate under tribocorrosion; (b) a smaller wear component (less mechanical removal due to a harder, more adherent film and higher near-surface work hardening); (c) a smaller corrosion component (lower steady-state corrosion current under sliding and faster current decay after perturbations); and (d) a reduced synergy term (the excess loss beyond the sum of separate wear-only and corrosion-only losses). The friction coefficient may decrease or remain similar; the key signature is faster repassivation (shorter current recovery time) with lower combined loss.
generation.baseline: Matched HEA of the same composition, grain size, and surface finish in the fully solutionized/random solid solution state, tested under identical tribocorrosion conditions.
generation.boundary: The prediction should hold for FCC HEAs with sufficient Cr to form a stable passive film under mildly oxidizing aqueous conditions and loads that do not catastrophically strip the film each cycle. It can fail in environments that prevent or dissolve stable chromia/spinels (e.g., strong reducing acids, concentrated fluoride at low pH), at temperatures or timescales that erase SRO, in HEAs with inadequate Cr, or under extreme contact conditions where mechanical removal always outpaces any possible repassivation.
generation.uncertainty: No prior evidence is supplied here, so effects are predicted qualitatively. The dominance of SRO versus other variables (e.g., grain size, second phases, Al-induced alumina formation) may be composition- and environment-dependent. Magnitudes of reduction in wear/corrosion cannot be confidently estimated without data; if hardness or third-body abrasion dominates, correlations to repassivation kinetics may weaken.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens with identical composition, grain size, and surface finish: (1) solutionized/random HEA (baseline) and (2) the same HEA aged to induce SRO, confirming SRO via diffuse scattering or atom probe indicators of local ordering. Measure (a) repassivation kinetics using electrochemical scratch or potential-step tests (track current transient decay time to baseline), (b) separate wear-only loss in an inert medium (e.g., dry or non-corrosive lubricant) at matched mechanics, (c) separate corrosion-only rate without sliding, and (d) total tribocorrosion mass loss under identical sliding in chloride solution. Compute the synergy term as total tribocorrosion loss minus the sum of separate wear-only and corrosion-only losses.
measurements: Repassivation time constant derived from current transient after scratching or potential steps in chloride solution
Steady-state corrosion current under sliding and at open circuit (or controlled potential)
Total mass loss under tribocorrosion (gravimetry or profilometry)
Wear-only mass loss in inert medium under identical mechanics
Friction coefficient and wear track microstructure/film hardness (nanoindentation on film)
Surface chemistry and oxide density/Cr enrichment (XPS/ToF-SIMS/TEM cross-sections)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SRO-enhanced specimen exhibits equal or faster repassivation (shorter current-decay time) yet shows equal or greater total tribocorrosion loss or an equal or greater synergy term compared to the solutionized baseline under matched conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
